question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ - \frac{99}{2}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ - \frac{99}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ - \frac{99}{2}\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ - \frac{99}{2}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-31 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{99}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} &=-3 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 5(1)+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 2{x}_{2} &=-19 \\ {x}_{2} &=- \frac{19}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{19}{2}$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{99}{2} \\ -(1)+3\left(- \frac{19}{2}\right) &=- \frac{99}{2} \\ - \frac{59}{2} &=- \frac{99}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=-20 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The first equation is a false statement. Hence, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}25 \\ 2 \\ -34\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}25 \\ 2 \\ -34\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}25 \\ 2 \\ -34\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}25 \\ 2 \\ -34\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=25 \\ -{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-34\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=-2$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=25 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(-2) &=25 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=9 \\ {x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-34 \\ -2(3)+4(-2) &=-34 \\ -14 &=-34\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
